messages.subject: adding symbols to plot.scanone plots?
messages.body_plain:
Does anyone know of a good way to add symbols ( i.e, arrows indicating
a marker that is significant in association scan etc) to the output of
plot.scanone? I would like to add arrows/symbols indicating other
genes of interest to a plot, not sure of an easy way to do this, any
suggestions?

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] adding symbols to plot.scanone plots?
messages.body_plain:
You can use arrows() to add an arrow.  The only tricky bit is getting
at the x-axis locations of various genomic positions in a scanone
plot, as the pasting of all of the chromosomes together (with gaps
between them), it's a bit confusing to figure out where 29 cM on chr 4
is, for example.

I'll add a utility function to help with this in the next version of
R; in the meantime, try something like the following code.

# scanone results for the hyper data
data(hyper)
hyper <- calc.genoprob(hyper, step=1)
out <- scanone(hyper)

# the chromosome lengths, and then the x-axis location for the start
of each chromosome for a given "gap" (default=25)
gap <- 25 # the default
L <- tapply(out[,2], out[,1], function(a) diff(range(a)))
start <- c(0,cumsum(L+gap))

# the chromosome names
thechr <- unique(out[,1])

# x-axis location for 29.5 cM on chr 4
x <- start[which(thechr=="4")] + 29.5

# plot scanone results
plot(out)

# add an arrow
ymx <- max(out[,3])
arrows(x+110, ymx, x+10, ymx, len=0.1, col="blue")

# add some text
text(x+120, ymx, "the peak", adj=c(0, 0.5), col="blue")

I hope this helps.

regards,
karl
